title: Tiger Milk Mushroom (Lignosus rhinocerus TM02) in Allergic Rhinitis: A Critical Reappraisal of the First Randomised Controlled Trial and the Human Evidence Base
content: The first randomised controlled trial of tiger milk mushroom (Lignosus rhinocerus TM02) in allergic rhinitis reported significant symptom relief associated with interleukin-5 downregulation. This review places that trial within the human evidence for the mushroom and reappraises its findings. Of 108 randomised patients, 52 (48%) were excluded from the main analysis, more from the TM02 arm (54%) than the placebo arm (43%). Unadjusted comparisons with placebo were not significant. Recalculated between-arm differences were 0.64 and 0.68 points on 15-point nasal symptom scores, with 95% confidence intervals of −1.15 to 2.43 and −1.03 to 2.39. Significant effects appeared only after adjustment for baseline immunoglobulin E in a full-interaction model; the reported standardised coefficients correspond to effects of 10 to 12 points, larger than the patients' baseline scores, consistent with a treatment coefficient evaluated at an immunoglobulin E level of 1 IU/mL. Interleukin-5 did not change in either arm. The trial was registered after the manuscript was submitted. The data support short-term tolerability but not efficacy. A prospectively registered, adequately powered trial with intention-to-treat analysis and prespecified, centred covariate adjustment is required before TM02 is recommended for allergic rhinitis.
